Subject-hash string format fragile; some columns not covered (not exploitable today: immutable/append-only).
User ids are compared exactly (now case-insensitively in the new separation checks). Safe only if the IdP issues one canonical id per person.
Lines appended *inside* the generating transaction are blocked at approval, leaving that journal stuck. Only the kernel's own transaction can do this.
The authenticity of a statement file depends on how it is obtained.
sum.golang.org, proxy.golang.org and vuln.go.dev are unreachable from the build workspace, so the official verification cannot run here.
Under ~6,000 concurrent calls the shared abuse store timed out for most calls and replicas fell back to local limits (stricter or looser by a few requests).

Budget relief is by cost code, not by the stock's origin (WAC stock is pooled): stock bought on one code and issued to another is charged to both (conservative: it refuses purchases, never allows an overspend).
Whoever controls the signer process or its secret controls approvals.
sum.golang.org, proxy.golang.org and vuln.go.dev unreachable from the build environment.
Signer limits: fixed per-process window (replicas multiply the budget); refusals counted, not rate-limited; MFA freshness decided by approval_authorize() (600 s).

After a quantity correction, ar_contract_position.certified_gross stays gross of the correction while measured_value is net, so 'certified > measured' can appear; retention and advance stay as certified (timing only).
